name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER5_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Steps in artificial hybridisation cross in pea

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps performed during an artificial cross-pollination (hybridisation) experiment in pea plants in the correct chronological sequence:

(i) Collection of seeds and raising the \(F_1\) progeny
(ii) Removal of anthers (emasculation) from the female parent flower
(iii) Selection of true-breeding parental pea lines with contrasting traits
(iv) Transfer of pollen (pollination) from the male parent to the stigma of the emasculated flower

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Controlled hybridisation in bisexual flowers like garden pea requires preventing self-pollination before introducing pollen from a chosen male parent.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering of Steps
First, true-breeding parental pea lines differing in contrasting traits must be selected. Second, anthers are removed (emasculation) from the bisexual flower designated as the female parent to prevent self-pollination. Third, pollen grains from the chosen male parent are transferred onto the stigma of the emasculated flower (pollination). Finally, the resulting pods mature and seeds are collected and sown to raise the \(F_1\) progeny.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is: Selection of true-breeding parental pea lines \(\rightarrow\) Emasculation \(\rightarrow\) Transfer of pollen \(\rightarrow\) Collection of seeds and raising the \(F_1\) progeny, which corresponds to (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER5_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Chronological milestones in classical genetics history

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following landmark discoveries and milestones in the history of genetics in the correct chronological order (from earliest to latest):

(i) Rediscovery of Mendel's results independently by de Vries, Correns, and von Tschermak
(ii) Publication of Mendel's work on the inheritance of characters in garden pea
(iii) Identification of the 'X body' during insect spermatogenesis by Henking
(iv) Formulation of the chromosomal theory of inheritance by Sutton and Boveri

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Tracing the historical timeline of classical genetics connects Mendel's mathematical rules of inheritance to cytological observations of chromosomes.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering of Milestones
Gregor Mendel published his work on the inheritance of characters in \(1865\). Later, in \(1891\), Henking traced a specific nuclear structure during insect spermatogenesis and named it the 'X body'. In \(1900\), three scientists—de Vries, Correns, and von Tschermak—independently rediscovered Mendel's results. Subsequently, by \(1902\), Walter Sutton and Theodore Boveri correlated chromosome movement during meiosis with Mendel's laws to formulate the chromosomal theory of inheritance.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Ordering these events from \(1865\) to \(1902\) gives: Publication of Mendel's work (\(1865\)) \(\rightarrow\) Identification of the 'X body' by Henking (\(1891\)) \(\rightarrow\) Rediscovery of Mendel's results (\(1900\)) \(\rightarrow\) Formulation of the chromosomal theory of inheritance (\(1902\)), corresponding to (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (i) \(\rightarrow\) (iv).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER5_SEQUENCING_Q03 - Causal sequence in sickle-cell anaemia pathology

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following molecular and cellular events leading to the phenotype of sickle-cell anaemia in the correct causal sequence:

(i) Polymerisation of mutant haemoglobin molecules under low oxygen tension
(ii) Single base substitution at the sixth codon of the \(\beta\)-globin gene from \(\text{GAG}\) to \(\text{GUG}\)
(iii) Change in the shape of the red blood cell from a biconcave disc to an elongated sickle-like structure
(iv) Substitution of Glutamic acid (\(\text{Glu}\)) by Valine (\(\text{Val}\)) at the sixth position of the \(\beta\)-globin chain

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive disorder that demonstrates how a point mutation at the DNA/mRNA level alters protein structure and ultimately changes cellular morphology.

Step 2: Causal Ordering of Events
The defect originates with a single base substitution at the sixth codon of the \(\beta\)-globin gene, changing the codon from \(\text{GAG}\) to \(\text{GUG}\). During translation, this altered codon causes the substitution of Glutamic acid (\(\text{Glu}\)) by Valine (\(\text{Val}\)) at the sixth position of the \(\beta\)-globin chain of haemoglobin. Under low oxygen tension, the resulting mutant haemoglobin molecules undergo polymerisation. This polymerisation deforms the red blood cell from its normal biconcave disc shape into an elongated sickle-like structure.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct causal sequence is: Single base substitution (\(\text{GAG} \to \text{GUG}\)) \(\rightarrow\) Amino acid substitution (\(\text{Glu} \to \text{Val}\)) \(\rightarrow\) Polymerisation of mutant haemoglobin \(\rightarrow\) Sickling of red blood cells, corresponding to (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (i) \(\rightarrow\) (iii).
